identity_notes: L-tryptophan's defining safety issue is the 1989 eosinophilia-myalgia syndrome (EMS) outbreak, traced to a contaminated batch of synthetic L-tryptophan from a single manufacturer, not the amino acid itself -- captured in 6 kept records (1369828, 1749939, 1829754, 1893558, 2331898, 15068828), all flagged for safety handoff. This is a manufacturing-contamination history, not an intrinsic-efficacy finding, and should not be conflated with dose-response efficacy claims. Genuine oral supplementation/efficacy evidence for L-tryptophan and its downstream metabolite 5-hydroxytryptophan (5-HTP, chemically related but distinct, flagged related_form_differs) is mixed to null across depression (350328, 779855, 794897, 7407745 -- all null or mixed vs placebo/active comparator), insomnia (6410442), running performance (1428380, null), and premenstrual dysphoria (10721042, positive). Two Cochrane-family systematic reviews (11687048, 11869656) and a meta-analysis (12169147) address tryptophan/5-HTP for depression, but the meta-analysis found only 2 of 108 identified studies met quality criteria (n=64 total) -- an extremely thin evidence base. A large fraction of retrieved records (>60) use the ACUTE TRYPTOPHAN DEPLETION paradigm, which REMOVES tryptophan via a tryptophan-free amino acid drink to study serotonergic function -- these are mechanistic/neuroscience research tools, not supplementation trials, and were rejected as not_intervention throughout. Many other records are probiotic/postbiotic/fermented-food RCTs where tryptophan metabolism is only a measured biomarker, not the administered substance -- also rejected. Several kept trials combine tryptophan or 5-HTP with other actives (magnesium, CoQ10, melatonin, mulberry leaf extract, pyridoxine) so the isolated tryptophan/5-HTP effect cannot be determined from those records. A notable number of retrieved abstracts were truncated before the results sentence in this scope, leaving several otherwise-relevant kept records (e.g. 25112175 postoperative delirium, 32067288/34403081 5-HTP in Parkinson's, 35940251 5-HTP in IBD fatigue) with direction_primary 'unresolved' -- the curator should re-pull full abstracts for these before drawing conclusions.
